T: Pines, crowding close. The town likes it that way.
M: The hill's rock face. An old fort is buried in it, wall and all.
Higher up, a rusted horn juts from the rock. At dusk it plays four cheerful notes.
The deserters hum along. They hate that they hum along.
E: The fort's arch, half swallowed by the hill. Cold air breathes out of it.
Carved above, half gone: "…LECREST SECOND REGIMENT…"
O: A boulder, wedged into a gap in the rock face. There's a space behind it.
Too heavy to move. It would take real strength to shift it.
Y: A child's wooden sword, worn smooth where a small hand held it.
A: A tent, patched more than it's tent. A plank by the flap reads NOT A DESERTERS' CAMP. Somebody has added, smaller: NOT ANY MORE. WE HAVE A CHAPEL NOW.
^: The farm track north, up the South Road to Warrior City.
_: The road south, toward the tithe camps and the old watchtower.
f: Turnips, beans and barley, in rows so straight you could rule a page with them. Everybody here farms. Everybody here prays for rain, and for something else.
H: A farmhouse. Over the door, a hand-painted sign: an open hand holding a sword by the blade.
D: You knock. An old voice, through the door: "Is it him? Is he back?" A pause. "Oh. Bless you anyway, dear."
d: The weaver's cottage. The door isn't locked. Through it, a trapdoor stands open, and there are voices underneath.
c: A candle in a lantern, burning steadily. Every house in Osric's Rest keeps one lit in the window, for when the prince comes home.
P: The chapel. Small, whitewashed, and full every evening. They pray for the harvest first, and then for him.
2: The chapel door. A carving over it: a crown, and under it, empty space, waiting.
W: The Candle Inn. A sign of a candle and the words WARM. FED. NOT ASKED.
6: The Candle Inn's door. The smell of soup, and somebody singing an old song about a prince, very quietly.

objects.name: Old Fen
lines: That fort isn't haunted.
Mess hall's haunted. Armoury's haunted. The drill yard's haunted by something that shouts. The rest is fine.

answer: Rooms, holes, ladders. More holes than a courier's socks.
Only one hole goes anywhere. The others go somewhere worse.
Behind that boulder in the rock, there's a gap. Found a child's toy sword in there once. Put it back.
Didn't feel like mine to take.
Terrified. Always have been.
Doesn't stop me walking. Just stops me walking fast.

questions.ask: You smell worse than the haunted mess.
answer: That's not me. That's the mess.
...Mostly not me.

lines: Under a tent peg marked NOT A TREASURE: a Heart Piece.
The deserters are very consistent about their signs.

objects.name: Bo Tumble
lines: Hup! Hup! Cartwheel number four thousand and nine!
Can't stop. If I stand still, it feels like the dream. So I don't.

answer: The long one. Everything soft, everything easy, forever.
I'd rather be dizzy.
The king's raiders at the checkpoint can be bought. Or bored into it. Wim loves a good story. Grask loves a good coin.
Because moving is how you know you're awake. Try it. Every day. Just a bit.

questions.ask: Stop flailing about. You look daft.
answer: Daft and awake!
Cartwheel four thousand and ten. That one was at you.

objects.name: Wim
lines: Oh good, company. It's been Grask, Grask and more Grask all week.
Did you know the king sleeps standing up? Like a horse? I'm almost sure.

answer: Watch the farmers for the king. Report anything odd.
Nothing's ever odd. Except the yarn. Somebody here gets through a LOT of yarn.

questions.ask: Are you scared of the king?
answer: Everyone's scared of the king. And chickens. Mostly chickens.
A goose came through last week. Collar said DUCHESS. Took Grask's helmet.
Grask cried. Grask says he didn't cry. Grask cried.

questions.ask: No wonder nobody tells you stories.
answer: That's a sad story. I didn't like that one.

objects.name: Grask
lines: Halt. Toll's everything you have.
You look like you've got nothing. Toll's double.

answer: ...Fine. The king says watch who comes in, not stop them.
Watching's free. I'm watching you now. Very hard.
Never. Wim says standing up, like a horse. Wim's an idiot.

questions.ask: Heard a goose made you cry.
answer: I didn't cry.
WIM! What have you been telling people?
WIM: Nothing! ...Everything.

lines: Beneath the smallest cairn stone, wrapped in a regiment scarf: a Heart Piece.
Somebody meant it for whoever came home. You'll do.

objects.name: Sergeant Bellow
lines: (whispering) Tithe camp. Fighters on the left. Iron on the right.
(whispering) Spoons are not iron. Tell Dobb. He won't hear it from me.
(whispering) I can't shout. Never could. The whole squad has to lean in. We're very close as a squad.

answer: (whispering) Born like it. My mum says I came out, looked around, and said 'oh no' very quietly.
(whispering) The horde made me a sergeant to toughen me up. Now everybody whispers back. It's quite nice.
(whispering) …There was no need for that.
(whispering) The whole squad heard. They're leaning away from you now. That's the worst thing we do.

objects.name: King's Guard
lines: Move along. No gathering. No praying in groups of more than three.
...Four's fine if one of you is a child. I don't make the rules.

answer: To make sure nobody here gets ideas. The king says a town that prays this much is planning something.
I've been here six years. All they've planned is turnips.
Rain, mostly. And some prince who's been gone five hundred years.
Nobody's told them he's not coming. I'm not going to be the one.
I'm guarding a turnip field against a rebellion of grandmothers.
Bored is the best day. Bored means nobody's hit me with a hoe.

objects.name: King's Guard
lines: Curfew's at the last bell. Lanterns out.
...They never put the lanterns out. Every window, every night. I've stopped writing it down.

answer: For the prince. So he can find his way home in the dark.
I asked a little girl why. She said, 'So he knows we waited.' I didn't write that down either.
The weaver gets through a lot of yarn for one woman. And there's a lot of digging at night, for a town that farms by day.
...It's turnips. It's always turnips.

questions.ask: Some guard. You can't even make them put a candle out.
answer: You try. Go on. Tell Nana Birch to put her candle out.
...I'll wait here. Somebody should be around to carry you back.

objects.name: Goodwife Ama
lines: Mind the rows, love. Barley this side, beans that side, hope down the middle.
We plant, we pray, we wait. My mother waited. Her mother waited. It's a family skill.

answer: The prince. Brannoc, Osric's boy. The one who was lost.
His regiment wrote him down as lost, not dead. Lost things can be found. We hold them to it.

questions.ask: Why is it called Osric's Rest?
answer: After the old king. Mad, they call him in the city. We called him ours.
When the shadow took him, his last soldiers walked out of the war and came here, and laid their swords down. So it's his rest, and theirs.
The guards think we're plotting. We're farming. Mostly.
Ask the weaver what she does with all that yarn. Actually, don't.

questions.ask: Five hundred years of waiting. He's not coming.
answer: Maybe not.
But if he does, and nobody's waiting, what sort of people would that make us?

lines: A little shrine of river stones between two candles. On it, a child's drawing of a man with a big beard and a small sword.
Under it, in many different hands: COME HOME. COME HOME. COME HOME.
Somebody has left him an apple.
